_comment: Cost per 1,000,000 (1M) tokens in USD. Two value forms: legacy 2-array [input, output], or object {input, output, cached_input, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h} for models where prompt-cache pricing matters (see forecaster.providers.resolve_price_detail — models without explicit cache fields get provider-default multipliers: claude cached 0.1x/write 1.25x-2x, gpt cached 0.1x, gemini cached 0.25x). One entry per model_id — lookup normalizes provider-prefixed forms like 'openai/gpt-5.4' automatically (see forecaster.providers.resolve_price_per_1m). When swapping a model in pythia/config.yaml llm.models, add its cost entry here; pythia/tests/test_model_registry.py enforces the sync. brave-web-search cost is per-query ($0.005), injected directly in usage dict — zero here to avoid double-counting. Superseded model ids are kept so a rollback via PYTHIA_SPD_ENSEMBLE_SPECS / SIBYL_MODEL still prices correctly. Batch API results are priced at 0.5x by the shared cost helper (usage service_tier=batch), not via entries here. Prices verified 2026-09-27: Anthropic against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (claude-opus-5-5 $4/$20, cache reads 0.05x = $0.20, 5m writes $5, 1h writes $8, batch $2/$10); OpenAI gpt-6-sol $2/$10 and gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50, cached input 0.1x, per the 2026-09-22 GPT-6 release (one report also gives Sol a $2.50 cache-write rate; OpenAI usage reports no cache-write token count, so no write price is recorded). The superseded gpt-5.6 entries follow: gpt-5.6-sol at the promotional $4/$20 in effect from 2026-08-21 through at least 2026-11-21 (list $5/$30 - restore it when the promotion ends), gpt-5.6-luna at $0.20/$1.20 since the 2026-07-30 price cut (was $1/$6), both with cached input at 0.1x. developers.openai.com is not reachable from the build sandbox, so the OpenAI figures rest on the OpenAI developer-community announcements and press coverage of these changes; re-check them on the pricing page.
